chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The women are inarticulate and exposed, therefore veil the exposure with the houses, and veil their inability to express themselves with the silence'.

key_terms.عَوْرَةٌ: Exposed part; vulnerability or modesty to be covered
key_terms.عَيٌّ: Inarticulate; one who cannot speak clearly or fully express themselves

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'women are inarticulate and exposed' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, reflects the Shia scholarly interpretation of gender dynamics through the dual concepts of 'awrah' (physical modesty) and 'ayy' (verbal or intellectual reserve). It instructs men to safeguard women's dignity by managing their physical visibility through domestic seclusion and their communicative expression through silence, emphasizing a protective rather than restrictive social framework. This teaching underscores the importance of modesty as a mutual social responsibility in maintaining familial and societal harmony.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umer, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The women are inarticulate and exposed, therefore veil the exposure with the houses, and veil their inability to express themselves with the silence’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib’iy ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, would offer Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) to women and they would respond in return and ’Amir al- Mu’minin would offer Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) to women but disliked to offer Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) to the young ones, saying, ’I am afraid their voice may attract me and make me feel negatively more than the reward I am seeking.’”
